content:
I have prepared a draft PR for the statement of the main results in the paper here: fpvandoorn/carleson#535
Let us use this thread to have an easier time discussing what should be in there or not.

From the PR:

Before putting more work into cleaning it up and a nice exposition, it would be nice to know if we are on the same page for what the 'main results' actually are.

I took it to mean:

  • metric space Carleson
  • linearised variant
  • two-sided variant

and also included:

  • classical Carleson
  • the specific 'real Carleson' instance used to make the derivation

In order to properly state everything I included a section with the definitions.

If anything else should be added, or something removed, please let me know.

Sorry for my late response.

Originally our plan was to state the results from Chapter 1, and also the results Propositions 2.0.1 - 2.0.4.
The latter requires us to define Grid/Tile/Forest/Antichain, so that we can talk about the design decisions for these, if there is anything interesting to say. This also allows us to give a brief proof sketch of the proof.

Very briefly:
Prop 2.0.1 => Th 2.1.1: by limiting arguments we may assume some additional finiteness/boundedness conditions
Prop 2.0.2 => Prop 2.0.1: we break up our space in small/nice pieces, both in the spacial dimension (given by Grid) and the frequency dimension (given by Tile)
proving Prop 2.0.2: there are 3 cases of tiles. The tiles where we can define "forests" are handled in Section 7 of the blueprint. Some tiles are handled by the antichain method from Section 6, and the remaining are the exceptional sets, handled in Section 5 itself.

Maybe writing out all 4 Propositions might be a bit much, so we can also decide to state 2 or 0 of them. What do you think?

We didn't originally plan on including real Carleson here. I don't mind including it. It might be even nicer in the motivation, before stating metric space Carleson, and use it as motivation, something like: "all proofs of Carleson theorem are done by showing that a Carleson operator is bounded. We have shown the following specific version of this result: <statement of real Carleson>".

Alright, that makes sense. I do think that it is most faithful to the effort of the formalization to give more of a proof sketch. My intuition would be to cover only 2.0.1 and 2.0.2, and subsequently comment on how one goes about proving 2.0.2 (the three cases you mentioned), highlighting that they are largely independent efforts with separate chapters in the blueprint.

I would include real Carleson as it is the bridge between the classical statement and the main result. I like the way you described it and will try to incorporate that.
As for the two propositions, my suggestion would be to put them in a separate section, giving the paper a bit more structure and allowing people to skip it if they are not interested.

I will proceed to make these changes. If you have other thoughts, please let me know.
